implemented: Preserves API v1 callable providers and adds API v2 object lifecycle: describe/can_edit/plan/candidate/persist/rollback. API v2 plans and persisted JSON descriptors are stored in the variant operation; replay rejects descriptor drift; candidate errors invoke the Provider compensation hook.
Provider JSON lifecycle outputs are finite, object-shaped and bounded to 64 KiB. Unsupported/conditional can_edit decisions fail closed with an actionable reason.

Adds path-based clone-selected and share-selected operations. Clone keeps copied parameters/buffers while breaking one named alias; share explicitly binds target paths to a source module. Default replace behavior still rebinds all aliases to one replacement.
Adds a guided workbench interaction for observed shared aliases, with operation preview, confirmation and variant persistence. Custom forward branch semantics remain owned by the Provider.
Updates the generated Provider scaffold to API v2 and adds a named-branch Provider example; increments Provider conformance-suite version and synchronizes Rust verification checks.

The interactive share-selected preview explicitly states that each target module and its parameters/buffers will be replaced by the source instance; clone-selected states that weights and buffers are copied.

limitations: Direct sharing operations use registered module paths; they do not infer custom forward control flow or semantic branch compatibility.
Fixture checks plus focused tests are finite evidence, not arbitrary-input correctness, general state migration, or commercial-value validation.
Provider Python can perform side effects outside the variant transaction; compensation is provider-owned and not an OS sandbox.
Provider Python executes with selected-interpreter permissions. rollback cannot reverse arbitrary filesystem/network/process side effects and is not an OS sandbox.
Shared-layer operations use declared module paths and do not infer arbitrary custom forward/control-flow semantics.
